cleanIntro: ⛔ THIS PISTOL COMES APART INTO MAJOR UNITS AND WALTHER TELLS YOU TO USE THAT. The GSP Expert's clean is not a wipe-down: "Take the pistol down to its main units from time to time." The strip needs an Allen key and it is ORDER-DEPENDENT — slide locking lever forward, upper part off, barrel locking screw slackened until the cocking-piece locking pin lines up with the hole in the slide casing, cocking knob out, hinged ejector open, barrel out, breech block out. The trigger unit is a REMOVABLE MODULE that comes out on one screw. ⚠ A .22 match barrel leads up rather than carbons up, and Walther's cleaning instruction is short and specific about it: bore from the rear, brass brush on the chamber, and OIL SPARINGLY — "excessive oiling promotes fouling."

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber checked, hammer down
steps.action: Remove the magazine and make sure no live round is left in the chamber. Then UNCOCK the pistol. The strip begins from a decocked gun, not from slide-locked-back.
steps.prose: Walther puts the chamber check in its own sentence with an exclamation mark. On a 5-round match magazine the count is easy and the chamber is the one that catches people out.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine. Make sure that no live round is left in the chamber! Uncock the pistol.
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.34
steps.warn: Never use force when using, stripping or assembling the weapon.

steps.title: Locking spring in, slide locking lever fully forward
steps.action: Push the locking spring on the slide locking lever (2) IN, and turn the lever fully forward. Fully — a lever left part way is what makes the next step feel jammed.
steps.prose: The spring is a detent. Pressing it is what lets the lever rotate at all, and it goes back the same way at the end.
steps.quote: Push the locking spring on the slide locking lever (2) in and turn the latter fully forward.
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.34

steps.title: Upper part forward about 7 mm, then straight up — and never face-down
steps.action: Push the upper part — barrel with slide — forward by about 7 mm and lift it off upward. The slide lock lever must be lying HORIZONTAL as you do it. No force. ⛔ Do not put the upper part down on its top side.
steps.prose: 7 mm is a real measurement, not an approximation to feel for: it is where the lugs clear. And the top-side rule protects the sights, which on the Expert are the moved-rearward set the variant is built around.
steps.aside: The slide lock lever must lie horizontally. Do not use force!
steps.quote: Push the upper part (barre1 with slide) forward by about 7 mm and lift off upward.
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.34
steps.warn: Do not put the upper part down on its top side.

steps.title: Barrel locking screw — slacken until the pin lines up with the hole
steps.action: With the Allen key, loosen the barrel locking screw (7) until the locking pin for the cocking piece lines up with the hole in the slide casing. This is an ALIGNMENT, not a number of turns — you are looking for the pin to appear in the hole.
steps.prose: Back it off until you see it. Going further does nothing useful and going less means the cocking knob will not come out in the next step.
steps.aside: cocking piece (see arrow) coincides with the hole in the slide casing.
steps.quote: Loosen the barre1 locking screw (7)with the Allen key until the locking pin for the
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.34

steps.title: Spring-loaded pin in, cocking knob out
steps.action: Push the spring-loaded pin inward and at the same time push the cocking knob (47) out. ⚠ The .32 S&W long version of this pistol needs an extra step here that this .22 does not — do not go looking for a knob screw you do not have.
steps.prose: Two hands, two directions, at the same moment. When the knob goes back in later, the liner has to point to the REAR.
steps.quote: Push the spring-loaded pin inward, at the same time pushing the cocking knob
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.35
steps.warn: When inserting the cocking grip, the liner (a) must point to the rear.

steps.title: Ejector open, screw out, barrel and breech block out
steps.action: Open the hinged ejector (8). Then loosen the barrel locking screw (7) further until the barrel can be withdrawn, and pull the breech block out of the slide casing.
steps.prose: The ejector is hinged — it swings, it does not come off. That is the gate that lets the breech block leave the casing.
steps.aside: can be withdrawn, then pull the breech block out of the slide casing.
steps.quote: Open the hinged ejector (8). Loosen the barrel locking screw (7) until the barrel
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.35

steps.title: Bore from the REAR, brass brush on the chamber lead
steps.action: Clean the bore FROM THE REAR END. Take the lead deposit out of the chamber with a brass wire brush. On a match .22 the chamber mouth is where the lead builds, and it is what changes how the gun chambers before it changes how it shoots.
steps.prose: Rear-entry is available because the breech block is out — which is the whole reason Walther says to take the gun to its main units from time to time rather than cleaning it assembled.
steps.quote: Clean the bore from the rear end. Remove the lead deposit from the chamber with a brass wire
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 14. Cleaning and care, printed p.39

steps.title: ⛔ Oil LIGHTLY — Walther says over-oiling causes the fouling
steps.action: Oil the pistol only lightly. Walther gives the reason in the same breath: excessive oiling PROMOTES fouling. On a rimfire that is literal — oil plus wax plus unburnt powder is a paste, and it collects exactly where the gun needs to be clean.
steps.prose: This is the single most-ignored line in match-pistol maintenance and it is printed right there in a two-sentence cleaning chapter.
steps.quote: Oil the pistol only lightly; excessive oiling promotes fouling.
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 14. Cleaning and care, printed p.39

steps.title: Rebuild — breech block, barrel, knob, ejector, in that order
steps.action: Reassemble in reverse and never use force. Re-insert the breech block in the slide casing, mount the barrel and tighten the barrel holding screw (7), then push in the cocking grip (47) — liner to the rear — and turn the ejector (8) back.
steps.prose: Tightening the barrel screw before the cocking grip goes in is the order that works. The other way round the pin is still sitting in the alignment hole.
steps.aside: barrel holding screw (7). Then push in the cocking grip (47) and turn the ejector back (8).
steps.quote: Re-insert the breech block in the slide casing. Mount the barrel and tighten the
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.37

steps.title: Upper part on 7 mm forward of closed, then back, then lever home
steps.action: Push the trigger unit firmly into the frame and lock it with the locking pin (3) — the point on that pin must then stand IN LINE WITH THE BARREL. Then place the slide casing on the frame about 7 mm FORWARD of the closed position, push it fully backwards, and turn the slide locking lever (2) fully home to the rear.
steps.prose: Same 7 mm as the strip, on the way in. The pin-point-in-line-with-the-barrel check is the one thing on this gun you can verify by eye before anything is loaded.
steps.quote: The point on the locking pin must then stand in line with the barrel.
steps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Stripping and assembling the pistol, printed p.37

deepSteps.title: The trigger unit is a MODULE — one screw and it lifts out
deepSteps.action: Turn screw (34) anti-clockwise. Hold the trigger unit at the DECOCKED hammer and remove it upwards, rotating it around the locking pin as it comes. This is a published, owner-level operation on this pistol — it is how the frame and the unit itself get cleaned.
deepSteps.prose: Holding it by the hammer is the instruction and it matters: that is the only place you can hold the unit without loading its own springs. Decocked first, always.
deepSteps.caution: Decock the pistol before the trigger unit is touched.
deepSteps.aside: remove it upwards by turning it around the locking pin.
deepSteps.quote: Turn screw (34) anti-clockwise, hold the trigger unit at the decocked hammer and
deepSteps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Removing the trigger unit, printed p.35

deepSteps.title: ⚠ The barrel weight normally STAYS ON — read this before you take it off
deepSteps.action: Walther's own guidance is that as a rule there is NO NEED to take the barrel weight off: when you clean the system, remove the barrel WITH the weight still attached. On the Expert that weight contains the recoil-dampening elements the variant exists for, so leaving it alone is the default and taking it off is the exception.
deepSteps.prose: This is the deep-clean step that is mostly about NOT doing something. Every removal of that weight is a front sight off and back on again.
deepSteps.caution: Default: barrel and weight come off together as one unit.
deepSteps.aside: system, remove the barrel along with the weight.
deepSteps.quote: As a rule, there is no need to take off the barrel weight. When you clean the
deepSteps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Removing the barrel weight, printed p.36

deepSteps.title: If it does come off — front sight first, then b, then slacken c
deepSteps.action: Take out the front sight screw (a) and lift the front sight off. Then remove screw (b) and loosen screw (c) by a few turns; the barrel weight can then come off. To put it back, reverse the steps — and make sure the threaded pin (c) ENGAGES IN THE RECESS at the bottom of the barrel.
deepSteps.prose: That recess is the whole location of the weight. If (c) is not in it the weight is clamped on friction, and on a gun built around damping mass that is a fault you feel on the second string.
deepSteps.aside: sight. Then remove screw (b) and loosen screw (c) by turning it a few times.
deepSteps.quote: If you nevertheless want to take off the barrel weight, remove the front sight screw (a) and lift off the front
deepSteps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Removing the barrel weight, printed p.36
deepSteps.warn: When doing so, make sure that the threaded pin (c) engages in the recess

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The damper screws (d) are a SETTING, not a cleaning step
deepSteps.action: Screws (d) adjust the spring force of the absorber weights and they are FACTORY SET. Clockwise increases the spring force, counter-clockwise decreases it. ⛔ Note where they were before you touch them, and treat this as a tuning decision made deliberately — not as something to reset because the gun was apart.
deepSteps.prose: This is the mechanism the Expert is named for. A clean is not a reason to move it.
deepSteps.caution: Factory set. Record the position before moving it, or leave it alone.
deepSteps.quote: Use screws (d) to adjust the spring force of the absorber weights (factory set).
deepSteps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 11. Removing the barrel weight, printed p.36

deepSteps.title: Cadence — what "from time to time" means for a high-round-count shooter
deepSteps.action: Walther gives no round count for this pistol; the instruction is "Take the pistol down to its main units from time to time." ⛔ That is the maker's cadence and it is not converted here into a number nobody published. What IS published is the stop condition: shooting ceases immediately on a visible defect in the pistol, or on extremely deformed or cracked casings.
deepSteps.prose: The honest reading is that the main-unit strip is the routine clean on this gun, not an annual event — that is why the strip chapter is four pages and the cleaning chapter is two sentences.
deepSteps.quote: Take the pistol down to its main units from time to time.
deepSteps.cite: Walther Bedienungsanleitung / Operating Instructions — GSP cal. .22 l.r. / GSP cal. .32 S&W long WC — 2505100.CW.08-13.0,5.21 (print code on the back cover — August 2013) — 14. Cleaning and care, printed p.39
deepSteps.warn: Occurrence of extremely deformed or cracked casings

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Bore cleaned FROM THE REAR — the breech block is out, use it
Brass wire brush on the chamber lead
Lead, not carbon, is what this barrel accumulates

cleaning.name: MAIN UNITS
tasks: Take the pistol down to its main units from time to time — Walther's own instruction
Barrel, breech block, slide casing, frame, trigger unit, magazine
⛔ Never rest the upper part on its top side

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: ⛔ Lightly, and no more — excessive oiling promotes fouling
Barrel weight normally stays on: clean the system with the barrel and weight together

reassembly: Breech block back into the slide casing.
Barrel mounted, barrel holding screw (7) tightened.
Cocking grip (47) pushed in — LINER TO THE REAR.
Trigger unit pushed firmly into the frame, locked with pin (3) — point IN LINE WITH THE BARREL.
Slide casing placed 7 mm forward of closed, pushed fully back.
Slide locking lever (2) turned fully home to the rear.
fncheck: Empty gun, magazine out. Before anything else, look at the locking pin (3) on the trigger unit: its point must stand in line with the barrel — that is Walther's own eye-check that the module is home. Then confirm the slide locking lever (2) is turned fully home to the rear and its locking spring has re-engaged, work the slide through its travel and lock it open on the catch, and check the hinged ejector sits closed. ⛔ If anything needs pressure, stop — Walther's rule for this pistol is that force is never used when stripping or assembling, and a part that will not seat is a part in the wrong place.
